title.narrative: Urgent food assistance to conflict-affected internally displaced people and logistics support to the broader humanitarian response in Lebanon

description.narrative: In addition to the deep economic crisis and political turmoil, the security situation in Lebanon has been worsening since the onset of the Gaza conflict in October 2023 and subsequent fire exchange along the Southern borders. To respond to the resulting humanitarian crisis, WFP has been on the ground supporting conflict-affected people through an assortment of assistance modalities, including in-kind parcels, emergency cash and in-school meals provided in schools hosting displaced students. In mid-September 2024, the conflict significantly escalated further, adding to the already alarming emergency situation in the country. According to the Lebanese authorities, more than 1,000 people lost their lives, over 6,000 have been injured, and an estimated one million people have been directly affected or displaced since October 2023. These figures are expected to rise, taking the ongoing emergency, which has already overwhelmed the nation’s resources and infrastructure, to a new level of humanitarian crisis. Following this further escalation, on 24 September 2024, WFP activated its emergency contingency plan and launched a large-scale response, reaching around 84,200 individuals with ready-to-eat (RTE) rations, cold and hot meals in 304 shelters and secondary residences across Lebanon as of 1 October. Emergency cash assistance was also distributed to 45,700 Lebanese individuals, primarily residing in the seven most impacted districts in southern Lebanon. The CERF contribution will enable WFP to further scale up and expand its ongoing emergency response through the procurement of additional much-needed RTEs to quickly respond to the immediate food needs of additional displaced people. The funds will enable WFP to purchase around 27,891 regional RTEs, allowing to cover the needs of 140,000 newly displaced persons (IDPs) hosted in shelters and host communities for 5 days. This intervention will cover the most urgent needs of affected populations in the immediate aftermath of their displacement and will help sustain their immediate food and nutrition needs. Designed to be consumed easily, these RTEs are composed of nutritionally balanced canned foods, including hummus, canned pulses, canned chicken, meat or tuna, canned vegetables and halawa/date bars, covering approximately 90 percent of the recipients’ daily kcal needs. Building on its role as lead agency of the Logistics Cluster, WFP also supports the provision of Common Services. Through this CERF allocation and at the request of the UN Country Team and partners, WFP will augment the current in-country logistics capacities to improve the effectiveness of the broader humanitarian response in Lebanon. Facilitation and optimization of supply chains, and personnel movements will, in turn, enable humanitarian agencies to be more effective in reaching and serving populations in need. Following the activation of the Logistics Working Group in Lebanon in 2023, coordination, convoy facilitation and information management roles were implemented. The current context requires additional and immediate augmentation of existing logistics capacity and coordination mechanisms. Informed by the ongoing Gaps and Needs Analysis, through the Logistics Cluster, WFP will support with coordination and information management services; common advocacy to address logistics bottlenecks; coordinate the movement of the humanitarian assistance through humanitarian corridors; establishment of common forward logistics bases for consolidation and prioritization of cargo; and support to cargo movement through dedicated fleet of trucks.
